data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise advanced use of determiners, pronoun reference and substitution across sentences and noun phrases.
learningPoints: Distinguish each, every, either, neither, both and all.
Use another, other, the other and others accurately.
Maintain clear pronoun and demonstrative reference.
Avoid ambiguous reference across clauses and sentences.
Choose determiners according to number, definiteness and contrast.

sections.explain: ANOTHER means one more or a different singular item; OTHER modifies plural or uncountable nouns.

words.word: Could I have another cup of coffee?
Could I have other cup of coffee?
Could I have an other cups of coffee?

sections.summary: Using 'the other' for the second of two.
sections.explain: THE OTHER refers to the remaining one of two known items.

words.word: One shoe is here, but I can't find the other.
One shoe is here, but I can't find another, meaning specifically the second of the pair.
One shoe is here, but I can't find other one the.

sections.explain: OTHERS functions as a pronoun and does not take a following noun.

words.word: Some people agreed; others disagreed.
Some people agreed; other disagreed.
Some people agreed; others people disagreed.

sections.explain: EITHER refers to one or the other of two alternatives.

words.word: Either option would be acceptable.
Every option would be acceptable, when only two are meant.
Either of option would be acceptable.

sections.summary: Using 'neither' for not one and not the other.
sections.explain: NEITHER means not either of two.

words.word: Neither answer is correct.
None answer is correct, when only two are meant.
Neither answers are correct in this singular determiner pattern.

sections.explain: EACH focuses on members individually; EVERY considers all members of a group one by one.

words.word: Each student received a different task.
Every students received a different task.
Each students received a different task.

sections.explain: ONE/ONES can replace a previously mentioned countable noun.

words.word: I prefer the smaller ones.
I prefer the smaller them.
I prefer smaller one, referring to several items.

sections.explain: THIS/THAT can refer back to a whole situation when the reference is clear.

words.word: The company cut prices. This led to higher sales.
The company cut prices. He led to higher sales.
The company cut prices. These led to higher sales, referring to one action.

sections.explain: A pronoun should clearly identify its antecedent.

words.word: When Maria spoke to Elena, Maria was upset.
When Maria spoke to Elena, she was upset, if the intended referent must be unambiguous.
When Maria spoke to Elena, it was upset.

sections.explain: ALL can come before THE/MY/THESE + noun.

words.word: All the students passed the exam.
The all students passed the exam.
All students the passed the exam.
